what_its_for: Trofinetide is used to treat Rett syndrome in adults and children 2 years of age and older. Rett syndrome is a rare brain disorder that affects development, movement, communication, and breathing. This medicine helps manage some of the symptoms of this condition.
how_to_take: Trofinetide comes as a liquid that you drink by mouth. Measure the dose carefully using the measuring device that comes with the medicine — do not use a regular kitchen spoon. You can take it with or without food. If your child has trouble swallowing, ask your doctor or pharmacist for tips. Do not mix it with other liquids or medicines unless your doctor tells you it is okay.
dosing: The dose is based on your child's or your body weight, so every person's dose may be different. Your doctor will tell you exactly how much to take and how often — usually twice a day, once in the morning and once in the evening. Always follow your doctor's instructions. Do not change the dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and just take the next one at the regular time. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store the unopened bottle in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C). Once you open the bottle, you can keep it in the refrigerator or at room temperature up to 77°F (25°C) for up to 28 days. Throw away any unused medicine after 28 days of opening the bottle. Keep the bottle tightly closed and away from children.
what_to_avoid: Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before taking any new medicines, including over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, or herbal supplements, because some medicines may interact with trofinetide. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel drowsy or dizzy after taking this medicine. Do not stop taking trofinetide suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you or your child experiences: severe or ongoing diarrhea (this is a very common side effect that can cause dehydration), signs of dehydration such as dry mouth, crying without tears, or dark-colored urine, nausea or vomiting that does not go away, significant weight loss, or any new or worsening symptoms. Seek emergency help immediately if there are signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: Trofinetide may not work right away. Some people may start to notice small improvements in symptoms over several weeks to months. Because Rett syndrome affects everyone differently, results can vary. It is important to keep giving the medicine as prescribed even if you do not see changes right away. Talk to your doctor regularly about how the medicine is working.
special_populations: Children: This medicine is approved for children aged 2 years and older. The dose is based on the child's weight, so follow your doctor's instructions carefully. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you or your child has kidney or liver disease, as the dose may need to be adjusted. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. It is not yet fully known how this medicine affects an unborn baby or breast milk. Your doctor will help weigh the risks and benefits.
